Professional Breast Volume & Weight Calculator — Pro cc/mL Tool for Clinicians & Fitters

Breast volume and weight can't be measured with a tape measure alone, but well-validated equations can give a reliable estimate from a few simple measurements. This hub gathers our breast volume calculator , breast weight calculator , and the underlying formulas so you can see exactly how the numbers are derived.

Both tools are based on peer-reviewed equations: BREAST-V (used by plastic surgeons), Qiao (the simplest two-input form), and Inami (which accounts for BMI). Use them as educational estimators, not medical devices.

What Is Breast Volume?

Breast volume is the three-dimensional space the breast occupies, measured in cubic centimeters (cc) or milliliters (mL). The two values are identical: 1 cc = 1 mL. Most adult breasts fall in the range of 50 cc to 1500 cc per breast , with the average around 250–400 cc.

Why does volume matter? It is the variable that determines how a bra cup actually fits, and it is the only direct measure of breast size that doesn't change with band measurement. Two people can both wear a 36C and have very different cup volumes depending on band length and breast shape.

What Is Breast Weight?

Breast weight is the mass of breast tissue in grams, calculated from volume times the density of breast tissue. Breast tissue is mostly water and adipose, so its density is close to 1.0 g/mL (1 cc ≈ 1 g). The simple shortcut is: cc ≈ grams for most estimates.

Breast weight is what determines how a bra band and straps have to support you. A 400 cc breast weighs roughly 400 g, and a 1000 cc breast can approach 1 kg. Over a day, that load adds up — this is why the band of a well-fitted bra carries 80–90% of breast weight, not the straps.

How the Calculators Work

Our breast volume calculator accepts four inputs — band, bust, frame size, and breast shape — and returns an estimate in cc with a confidence range. Our breast weight calculator takes the same inputs and converts the volume to grams using a tissue density of 0.9–1.0 g/mL.

Under the hood, the tools use a layered approach:

  1. Qiao (2009) — single-input form using band and bust only. Good for a quick estimate, ±20%.
  2. Inami (1995) — adds height, weight, and BMI. More accurate for body-shape outliers.
  3. BREAST-V (Longo et al., 2013) — best validated; includes breast base width. Best for surgical planning contexts.

How to Measure for the Calculator

You will need a soft measuring tape and, ideally, a mirror. Three measurements are required for the most accurate estimate:

  1. Band (underbust): snug, directly under the breasts. Round to the nearest inch.
  2. Bust (overbust): loose, at the fullest part of the breast. Round to the nearest inch.
  3. Frame: optional but helpful. Measure at the fullest part of the hips for hip-to-bust ratio input.

For the BREAST-V formula, also measure breast base width — the horizontal distance from the inner to the outer edge of the breast footprint on the chest wall. This is the most under-measured input and the one that introduces the largest error if guessed.

Accuracy & Limitations (YMYL Disclosure)

This tool is for educational and informational purposes only . It is not a medical device, is not intended to diagnose or treat any condition, and should not be used as a substitute for consultation with a qualified healthcare professional.

Volume estimates from these formulas are typically within ±15% to ±20% of MRI-measured volume for most adults. The error increases for people who are very lean, very overweight, or have had breast surgery. If you need a precise measurement for surgical planning, ask a plastic surgeon about Vectra 3D imaging or MRI-based volumetry.

Frequently Asked Questions

How accurate is the breast volume calculator?

For most adults, the calculator is within ±15–20% of MRI-measured volume. Accuracy drops at the extremes of body weight, after breast surgery, and during pregnancy or lactation.

Is breast volume the same as bra cup size?

Not directly. Two people with the same bra size (e.g., 36C) can have different breast volumes because the band length affects cup size letters. A 36C and a 38B have different bands but can have similar cup volume if the band-to-bust ratio is preserved.

How much does a 36C breast weigh?

A 36C breast typically weighs about 280–350 g per breast, so 560–700 g total. Cup-letter estimates like these are averages; use the calculator for a personalized estimate.

Does this calculator work after breast surgery?

It can, but accuracy is reduced. The Qiao and Inami formulas were derived from non-surgical populations. For post-mastectomy planning, see our post-mastectomy care guide .

Is breast density a factor?

Yes. Dense breast tissue has a slightly higher density than adipose tissue, but the difference (5–10%) is within the calculator's margin of error. If you have a recent mammogram, dense breasts are visible there, but this calculator doesn't require that data.
